newsitem.title: USA: Rubin still sees continued growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin still sees continued growth, low inflation.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin Sunday repeated his outlook for solid U.S. economic growth with low inflation for the foreseeable future.
"I think the most likely outcome going forward is a continuation of solid growth and low inflation, Rubin said on CBS's Face the Nation.
The stock market, which is currently on a extended bull run, has many investors committed to holding positions for the long-term, prepared to weather any market correction.
However, Rubin said, "The level of the stock market, is something I've never chosen to comment on."
Although "the question is, at any given moment in time, is the market over valuing, over valued, rightly valued, or under valued," Rubin said.

A survey released February 21 by Nasdaq showed 63 percent of investors expect stock prices to rise over the next 12 months and 54 percent would not make major changes to their stock holdings in the event of a significant market decline.
The Dow Industrials rose four points to close unofficial Friday at 6931 after a day virtually devoid of the market's recent volatility.
